text: What happens inside me during a period?

steps.title: An example period
steps.say: I've put an example period on your copy: today is day 2. It begins in the ovary, where last month's empty follicle has stopped making progesterone.

steps.title: The lining loses support
steps.say: Progesterone was keeping the thick, blood-rich lining ready for a pregnancy. With no pregnancy, it drops, and the lining can no longer hold on.

closeup.basis: Textbook menstrual cycle: progesterone and lining peak in the late luteal phase, before falling

steps.title: Shedding
steps.say: The small arteries feeding the lining clamp down, the starved top layer breaks away, and it leaves with some blood as your period. The deep layer stays to regrow.

steps.title: Why it cramps
steps.say: The breaking lining releases prostaglandins. They make the uterus muscle squeeze to push the lining out, and squeezing briefly cuts its blood supply, which hurts.

composed.caption: Prostaglandins make the uterus muscle squeeze
composed.basis: Textbook physiology of primary dysmenorrhea: prostaglandin-driven contraction and reduced blood flow; amounts are illustration

steps.title: The next round starts
steps.say: While you bleed, the brain's signal is already waking a new follicle, so a fresh egg starts ripening and estrogen will soon rebuild the lining.

steps.title: The rest of you
steps.say: With progesterone gone, your body runs a touch cooler, around 36.7 °C now, and handles sugar a little more easily than before the period.

lines.text: No pregnancy means progesterone falls, so the uterus sheds its top lining with some blood.
Prostaglandins make the uterus squeeze the lining out, so you may feel cramps.
A new egg starts ripening and the lining regrows. This is a typical example cycle.
